clue.text: Affording great opportunities, musical wealthy businessmen produced

parts.note: a fat part or job is one rich in openings; Chambers gives this sense

explanation.surface: A lucrative stage musical has made its backers rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affording great opportunities' reads as describing the musical, but it is the clue for the first word, as in a fat role for an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for rich, powerful executives and financiers, a synonym for wealthy businessmen.

clue.text: View of expert opposite

parts.note: to face a scene is to look out on it
'of' and 'to' swap in phrases like the key of, or to, the door
an ace is an expert; the leading F has no word of its own in the clue

explanation.surface: An expert's view of the other side of a question.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half needs F plus ACE, but only 'expert' (ACE) is printed, so the clue as published leaves the F unexplained.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people sitting face to face are directly across from each other, so the phrase is a synonym for opposite.

clue.text: Article on extremely miserable topic

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the following word, its first and last letters only

parts.note: the two end letters of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written on a deeply depressing subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic that a piece of writing or talk deals with.

clue.text: Against carrying on — old Shakespearean merchant

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old merchant is told to stop carrying on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like one phrase meaning continuing; split it, so 'carrying' holds the word on inside the word for against.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio is the title character of The Merchant of Venice, Shakespeare's best-known merchant.

clue.text: Where money may be held in cliffhanging tale?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bookkeeping account where sums are parked until their proper home is known
second meaning, read playfully: a story or account full of suspense

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, whimsical reading: an account can be a story, and a cliffhanger is full of suspense.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, a suspense account temporarily holds sums that cannot yet be allocated, so money is literally held there.

clue.text: … we also back cowboy film

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: The leading dots continue the previous clue: we too support a cowboy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the verb to support, but it is a noun for the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a film genre set in the American Old West, typically with cowboys as heroes.

clue.text: And the enemy bombed seaport sooner than expected

indicators.note: something bombed has been blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: time is proverbially the enemy, as in 'time, the old enemy'

explanation.surface: A wartime report: the enemy has bombed a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is the stock phrase for time, which runs out on us all.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving with time to spare means getting there early, before the deadline or expected moment.

clue.text: Short game fish

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a hide-and-seek party game in which seekers squeeze in beside the hider

explanation.surface: A curt instruction about some brief game of fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game fish' looks like the sporting-fish phrase, but 'game' belongs to the wordplay and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Repent wildly about glacier where maximum damage may occur

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one set of letters goes around another
acting wildly means out of control, so the word's letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a glacier is a river of ice

explanation.surface: A warning to repent before the glacier wreaks havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface above an earthquake's origin, where shaking and destruction are usually greatest.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née, born, introducing a maiden name
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A short life story: born poor and died poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of want or destitution is a synonym for poverty, as in families living in need.

clue.text: Talk about conclusion to bizarre con

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk word is wrapped around a letter
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Discussing how a strange swindle ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To con someone is to cheat them, swindling them by trickery.

clue.text: Dark planet that is seen around noon

indicators.note: seen around means placed so as to surround, putting one letter inside

parts.note: 'that is' gives i.e., id est; here 'that' is the link and 'is' the abbreviation's cue
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes a dark planet visible around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' together gives the abbreviation I.E., which goes around the N for noon after Saturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy, sullen, dark in temperament, from the old belief in Saturn's melancholy influence.

clue.text: Play a ragtime piece

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John Osborne's 1957 stage play about a failing music-hall comic
second meaning: Scott Joplin's 1902 piano rag, made famous again by The Sting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as an instruction to perform the ragtime number, but it is a separate definition: the title is shared by a drama and a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The same title belongs to both Osborne's drama and Joplin's rag, so each half of the clue names one of them.

clue.text: House plant in a pot I set out

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the preceding letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: put the plant in a pot that I set out.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia, with red bracts, is a popular indoor plant, especially at Christmas.

clue.text: Female film stars bringing agents

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Actresses arriving with their agents in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agents' suggests the stars' representatives, but here it means things or people that bring something about, or business agents.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an agent, either one who does business for another or a contributing cause.

clue.text: Is working within to copy enamelware

indicators.note: within means inside, so the first words go inside the copy word

parts.note: a clone is an exact copy
IS taken as written plus ON, working or operating

explanation.surface: Someone is busily reproducing a piece of enamel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is decorative enamel work in which colours are separated by thin metal strips.

clue.text: Distinguished conductor from Rome sat nervously

indicators.note: acting nervously means fidgeting, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A famous conductor visiting from Rome sat on edge before the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is the honorific for an eminent conductor or musician, borrowed from Italian for master.

clue.text: Reportedly catch a bacterial disease

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so we go by sound not spelling

parts.note: to collar someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: It is said that you can easily catch a germ-borne illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests catching an illness, but it is the police sense: to collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious intestinal illness caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.

clue.text: Add to first of eggs? Hen can, conceivably

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken
conceivably means in some imaginable form, so the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Can a hen boost the egg count? Possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceivably' doubles as a joke on what a hen conceives: eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to augment or improve it, adding to its value or quality.

clue.text: Article used in part exchange rated badly at one's place of business

indicators.note: done badly means jumbled, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: someone at their office or shop is in

explanation.surface: A shop valued your old item poorly when you swapped it for a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old item handed over as partial payment toward a new one.

clue.text: Stinging insect moving many in painting

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled letters sit within the other word
moving means shifting position, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A painting shows a swarm of stinging bugs on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants are tropical ants that march in huge columns and sting or bite prey.

clue.text: A second teaches differently, perhaps, depending on the particular circumstances

indicators.note: doing something differently means not in the usual way, so the letters take another order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A deputy teacher teaches in a different way, perhaps, depending on the class.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means according to whichever situation applies, i.e. conditionally on circumstances.

clue.text: Long story about last in clubhouse

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story word wraps a letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tall tale

indicators.note: last in means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An old member spins a lengthy tale in the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective describing the story, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, the two verbs being synonyms for strong desire.

clue.text: Brought up plans for junk mail

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Plans are raised at a meeting about unsolicited mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the everyday name for unwanted bulk email, a modern synonym for junk mail.

clue.text: Strip of land shot in pale sun

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: A photo of a stretch of coast taken in weak sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is a narrow piece of land jutting into water, almost an island.

clue.text: Not together in a district

parts.note: a district is a part of a town or region

explanation.surface: Living separately within one neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated, at a distance from one another, the opposite of together.

clue.text: Actress, after having stitch in side, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the whole is read right to left
in means placed inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: An actress comes back after a painful stitch in her side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch in side' reads as the running cramp; side is a sports team here, with the sewing word put after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was an American stage and film actress famed for her innuendo-laden lines.

clue.text: Land in Preston I acquired

indicators.note: in means contained within, so letters are taken from inside the next word

parts.note: the tail of the place name
A is a listed abbreviation for acquired

explanation.surface: A northerner boasts of buying land in Preston.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston is a town in Lancashire, north-west England; its last five letters start the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, and land is a common crossword word for a country.
